newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Palestinian envoy opens fire on Indonesian thief.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian envoy opens fire on Indonesian thief.

text.p: Palestinian Ambassador to Indonesia Ribhi Awad fired at a man who was trying to rob him after helping to change a flat tyre, shooting him in the foot, the envoy said on Thursday.

The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted Awad as saying he was unaware he had hit the man during the incident on Tuesday night as he was only trying to scare him away. The man was later taken into custody by police at a west Jakarta hospital.
"I never, ever intended spilling even one drop of Indonesian blood," Awad was quoted as saying by the newspaper.
Awad told Reuters on Thursday that the newspaper report was correct, but refused to give details.
The Post said the incident took place about 9:15 p.m. near the Philippine embassy in the plush central suburb of Menteng, less than one km (half a mile) from Awad's mission and residence.

It said Awad's limousine had a flat tyre and that a man, identified as Hariyanto, helped him change the tyre. He refused an offer of 20,000 rupiah ($7.70) for his help and instead pulled out a knife in an apparent robbery attempt as the ambassador got back into the car.
Awad fired at him with a handgun, it said.
"I didn't know I hit his foot because I didn't try to shoot him. I just wanted to shock him," Awad said.
Police said the incident, reported on the front page of most Indonesian newspapers, was being investigated.
"He is an ambassador, but has proved himself a marksman," the English-language Indonesia Times said.
